title.narrative: Transforming Landscapes for Resilience and Development in Zambia

description.narrative: The development objective of the Transforming Landscapes for Resilience and Development Project for Zambia is to improve natural resource management in select districts to support sustainable livelihoods, and in the event of an eligible crisis or emergency, to provide immediate and effective response to the eligible crisis or emergency. There are four components. First component, Promoting Diversified, Resilient, Sustainable Livelihoods is designed to create conditions for poverty-stricken communities facing climatic impacts to strengthen their resilience.This component also supports ward-level development planning, TA, workshops, and trainings for capacity building and institutional development.The activities under this component are structured around the following tasks: (a) increase smallholder production and productivity, (b) mitigate farmers risks through the adoption of new technologies, and (c) facilitate adoption of alternative livelihoods as sustainable and resilient initiatives with reduced reliance on natural resources.This component also aims to support and improve infrastructure in vulnerable areas suffering from the lack of investments and that are also adversely affected by climate change.This component has four sub-components. (i) Diversifying Livelihoods and Improving Farming Practices; (ii) Developing Productive Climate Resilient Infrastructure for Sustainable Livelihoods; (iii) Strengthening Communities and Expanding Services; and (iv) Strengthened Climate Hydro-meteorological Information; Second component, Management of Community Forests and Protected Areas supports the establishment of Community Forest Management Group (CFMGs) as well as Natural Forest Regeneration (NFR) areas to more effectively manage available forests and to create the minimal necessary conditions for restoring degraded forest areas. The component also addresses the problem of insufficient funding of the established Protected Area (PAs) in the Luapula, Muchinga, and Northern (LMN) Provinces. Main activities include developing basic infrastructure and strengthening capacity and management to protect and preserve biodiversity and ecosystem services. The component design and activities targeted under this component are consistent with the strategy developed by the Government of the Republic of Zambia (GRZ) for tourism development and support the implementation of the Zambia Tourism Master Plan approved in 2018.It has two sub-components. (i) Community Forest Management and Natural Forest Regeneration and (ii) Improved Management of Protected Areas (PAs); Third component, Project Management, Coordination, and Monitoring will finance the establishment and activities of three Provincial Project Implementation Units (PPIUs), TA, works, goods, services, workshops, and operational costs to support the project's day-to-day implementation and management, including procurement, financial management (FM), environmental and social safeguards, and preparation of annual work plans and organization of audit reports; and Fourth component, Contingency Emergency Response Component had been embedded in the project to finance early recovery and/or specific emergency works, goods, and services in case of eligible emergencies or crises or disasters caused by natural or man-made hazards, including public health crisis.

To improve natural resource management in select districts to support sustainable livelihoods, and in the event of an eligible crisis or emergency, to provide immediate and effective response to the eligible crisis or emergency.

condition.narrative: Institutional Arrangements. 1. The Recipient, through MNDP, shall maintain, throughout the period of implementation of theProject, the National Project Coordinating Unit (“NPCU”) with a mandate, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association– Financing Agreement Section I.A.1 of Schedule 22. By no later than two (2) months after the Effective Date, the Recipient shallestablish and therefore maintain, throughout the period of implementation of the Project, in each of the Project Provinces, thefollowing bodies: (a) the Provincial Project Implementation Unit and the Provincial Planning Sub-Committee (“PPSC”), with amandate, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association - Financing Agreement Section I.A.2(a, b) of Schedule 23. TheRecipient shall maintain, throughout the period of implementation of the Project, in each of the Project Provinces, with a mandate,composition and resources satisfactory to the Association (a) the District Planning Office; and (b) the District PlanningSub-committee - Financing Agreement Section I.A.3(a, b) of Schedule 24. The Recipient shall establish and thereafter maintain,throughout the period of implementation of the Project, in each of the Project Provinces, with a mandate, composition and resourcessatisfactory to the Association, the Ward Development Committee - Financing Agreement Section I.A.4) of Schedule 2

Participation Agreements.Prior to financing any Project activities under Parts 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2 and 3(b) of the Project out of theproceeds of the Financing, the Recipient shall enter into, and thereafter maintain throughout the period of implementation of theProject, a Participation Agreement with each Project Province under terms and conditions acceptable to the Association- FinancingAgreement Section I.B.1 of Schedule 2

Priority Adaptation Sub-projects. For purposes of the proper implementation of activities under Part 1.1 of the Project, theRecipient, through the Project Provinces, shall provide Small Grants to Selected Farmers to finance Prior Adaptation Sub-projectsin accordance with this Agreement and with the selection criteria, guidelines and procedures set forth in the ProjectImplementation Manual -Financing Agreement Section I.D.1 of Schedule 2

Safeguards1. The Recipient shall ensure and cause to ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance with the provisions ofthe ESMF, the PMP, the RPF, the PF and all Safeguard Assessments and Plans and the requirements of the Grievance Redress Mechanism-Financing Agreement Section I.F.1 of Schedule 22. If any activity under the Project would involve Affected Persons, theRecipient shall: (a) ensure that no displacement (including restriction of access to legally designated parks and protected areas)shall occur before resettlement measures under the relevant Safeguard Assessment and Plan prepared in accordance with the RPF,including, in the case of displacement, full payment to Affected Persons of compensation and of other assistance required forrelocation, have been implemented; and (b) provide from its own resources, any financing required for any measures undersub-paragraph (a) above including any costs associated with land acquisition required for the Project - Financing Agreement SectionI.F.2 of Schedule 23. Without limitation on its other reporting obligations under this Agreement, the Recipient shall collect,compile and submit to the Association on a bi-annual basis (or such other frequency as may be agreed with the Association)consolidated reports on the status of compliance with the ESMF, the PMP, the RPF, the PF and the Safeguard Assessments and Plans,giving details of: (a) measures taken in furtherance of the said instruments; (b) conditions, if any, which interfere or threatento interfere with the smooth implementation of the said measures; and (c) remedial measures taken or required to be taken toaddress such conditions- Financing Agreement Section I.F.3 of Schedule 2

comment.narrative: The 126 km target was met following the completion of the 39 km Buyantanshi channel in Lunga district, Luapula Province.

title.narrative: Female led Community Forest Management groups

comment.narrative: This result fell short of the target with only 40% achievement largely due to gender gaps, as most of the CFMGs were dominated by men.

This indicator is defined as “Carbon stock changes per unit of land, expressed in tCO2-eq per hectare and year as a result of project activities to establish Community Forest Management Groups and Natural Forest Regeneration areas”, while its unit of measure is metric ton (mt). The original target of 6,832,864 mt was revised strongly upwards to 32,305,476 mt in the first project restructuring after the Mid-Term Review in June 2023, when the indicator gave result of 22,472,515 mt. The same remains the end result, achieving only 69.6% of the revised target. TRALARD having been a demanding project with numerous different work fronts, timely final measurement of this indicator for the project closure got unwillingly omitted. The final result will be measured for the ICR.

The project end target of 30 CFMGs established was reached and surpassed by 103.3%. At the project closure, the Forestry Department (FD) under the Ministry of Green Economy and Environment (MGEE) produced an assessment report on the 31 CFMGs to monitor and assess the status of their Community Forest Areas (CFAs) along with the capacity and sustainability of the CFMGs. The report provided valuable insights and lessons learnt to be incorporated in an increasing CFMG work under TRALARD II.

title.narrative: Farmers reached with agricultural assets or services

comment.narrative: This indicator aggregates the number of farmers who were provided with agricultural assets or services as a result of TRALARD support. "Agriculture" or "Agricultural" includes: crops, livestock, capture fisheries, aquaculture, agroforestry, timber, and non-timber forest products. Assets include property, biological assets, and farm and processing equipment. Biological assets may include animal agriculture breeds (e.g., livestock, fisheries) and genetic material of livestock, crops, trees, and shrubs (including fiber and fuel crops). Services include research, extension, training, education, ICTs, inputs (e.g., fertilizers, pesticides, labor), and production-related services (e.g., soil). This indicator also captures beneficiaries from water harvesting facilities, cleared transportation channels, weirs and irrigation canals, crossing points, and embankments.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries with access to improved/new infrastructure

comment.narrative: The target was not met largely due to the cancellation of key infrastructure activities following the cancellation of the US$12.8 million funding. The cancelled infrastructure included three weirs and irrigation canals in Northern Province and three bulking centers in Luapula Province.

This indicator reports the NFR areas established for restoration/rehabilitation of degraded land areas in especially designated NFR areas, surpassing the target by 101.4%. It is to be noted that the indicator does not cover NFR taking place on degraded areas within the 31 beneficiary Community Forest Areas (CFAs).

title.narrative: Area provided with new/improved irrigation or drainage services

comment.narrative: All the planned irrigation and drainage services have been completed. This result is an aggregate of land area in hectares provided with both new and improved irrigation and drainage services. This includes irrigation area under solar-powered boreholes. About 84% of this result is covered by drainage services.

title.narrative: Share of women participants in Savings and Credit clubs

comment.narrative: Percentage of women participating in savings and credit clubs

title.narrative: Beneficiaries participating in CFM and NFR groups

comment.narrative: This result fell short of the target with only 50.3% achievement due to overall low levels of interest among community members during the early TRALARD stages when the CFMGs were being established. Additionally, some community members and traditional leaders were initially reluctant to participate, as the concept of Community Forest Management (CFM) was relatively new and there were concerns regarding land governance. A key lesson learned is the need for enhanced and more sustained community engagement, particularly with traditional leaders, who play a critical role in awareness raising and mobilization for CFM and NFR.

title.narrative: Improved hydromet system rehabilitated and/or newly installed

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the number of automated weather stations (AWS) in the network of the Zambia Meteorological Department (ZMD) providing data ingested to the climate data management system on a single day, computed as a 30-day running average. During 2025, the project focus moved from the reported installation of a total of 135 AWS to a count of the AWS for which the indicator success could be established, namely AWS reporting to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO). In late December, the relevant AWS observed on the WMO website as successfully reporting are 74 on average, exceeding the indicator target by 123.3%. Contract completion reports on the installed AWS indicate that up to 135 AWS could report to ZMD headquarters, but the only feasible and certain way to verify success of data collection and transmission is based on the AWS reporting to the WMO. World Bank's Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR) will analyze this indicator further.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries reporting satisfaction with key aspects of collaboration process

comment.narrative: This indicator was estimated using the Citizen Engagement and Household Beneficiary Impact Assessment, finalized in the first quarter of 2025.

This result is the total number of farmers practicing climate-smart agriculture (CSA). It includes farmers supported under community subprojects, Individual Champions, farmers implementing livelihood activities under CFMGs, and those supported by irrigation canals/schemes.

title.narrative: Households adopting diversified livelihood activities supported by the project

comment.narrative: This result is the total number of households (HH) practicing CSA. It includes HH supported under community subprojects, Individual Champions, HH implementing livelihood activities under Community Forest Management Groups (CFMGs) as well as HH supported by irrigation canals/schemes.

title.narrative: Forest area brought under management plans

comment.narrative: The result presents 237,297 ha of Community Forest Management Areas and the 150,000 ha of the Lavushi Manda National Park. The partial 73.8% achievement of the target is due to the Department of National Parks and Wildlife (DNPW) not getting to finalize an update of the General Management Plan (GMP) of the Lusenga Plains National Park (LPNP), which was aborted after completion of the baseline. In every case, DNPW will continue to implement LPNP management activities as law enforcement, ecological monitoring and grading of park and loop roads in line with the latest GMP until a successor plan is prepared. In both NPs, the completed investments include construction of staff houses and a park gate, delivery of field equipment and training, road grading, community outreach, and field operations. In LMNP, also a boma was constructed and the boundary marked. Some activities as wildlife restocking got cancelled and partly initiated activities as the LPNP boundary marking were not completed.

title.narrative: Land area under sustainable landscape management practices

comment.narrative: This indicator and result cover (i) agriculture land under climate-smart agriculture (CSA) practices (conservation agriculture, crop rotation, use of certified seeds, organic fertilizer, and animal manuring, intercropping, agroforestry, and crop diversification, among others) implemented on and off-season with support of solar powered boreholes and irrigation canals beyond rainfed agriculture; (ii) the 31 Community Forest Areas (CFAs) under sustainable management, covered by management plans; and (iii) the 150,000 ha area of the Lavushi Manda National Park (LMNP) covered by an updated General Management Plan (GMP) and a new Business Plan.
